rationale: A shows a stable play-ball focus, reacts strongly to TOUCH (t8), OFFER_FOOD (t32), and STARTLE (t68), but shows little change to CALL (t20) or PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL (t44), then spends long spans standing with attention=NONE (t40–67, t72–95). B exhibits richer, coherent engagement: shifts from PERSON_BETA to PERSON_ALPHA on TOUCH (t8), maintains social focus with vocalization (t18–19), makes spontaneous but sensible shifts (e.g., to AVERSIVE_BUZZER at t30–31, to PLAY_CUBE at t42, to PLAY_CHIME at t54, back to PLAY_CUBE at t66), responds promptly to OFFER_FOOD (t32) and PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL (t44), startles and withdraws (t68–71), then recovers into varied play (t78–83, t94–95). This demonstrates higher autonomy, coherence, adaptation, and spontaneous activity.
